fatal_errors: The proposed NiTi shape-memory alloy is unrelated to the target FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based medium-entropy alloy single crystals.

The hypothesis substitutes an austenite-to-martensite phase-transformation mechanism for the target mechanisms of thermally activated dislocation glide, cryogenic inertial dulling, lattice-distortion strengthening, and high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier pinning.
It does not reconstruct the target compression tests, crystallographic orientation, CRSS measurements, strain-rate jumps, temperature range, or composition-dependent comparisons.
explanation: The response addresses temperature-dependent deformation only at a very broad level. Its material, treatment, structural mediator, mechanism, conditions, and predicted outcomes do not agree with the target study. The proposed controlled comparison, DSC, mechanical testing, TEM, and explicit falsification rule provide some experimental discriminability, but the baseline and boundaries remain vague and no quantitative test conditions or evidence are supplied. As a standalone NiTi hypothesis it is conceivable, but it is neither an evidence-supported alternative nor a reconstruction of the target.
